verses.text: When Samuel grew old, he made his sons judges over Israel.
His oldest son was named Joel and his second son Abijah. They served as judges at Beersheba.
But his sons did not live the way he did. They were greedy for money. They took bribes and twisted justice.
So all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.
They said to him, "You are old, and your sons do not live the way you do. Now give us a king to lead us, like all the other nations have."
But when they said, "Give us a king to lead us," Samuel was unhappy. So he prayed to the LORD.
The LORD told him, "Listen to everything the people are saying to you. It is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected me as their king.
They are doing to you what they have done from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until now. They have left me and served other gods.
So listen to them. But warn them seriously, and let them know what the king who rules over them will do."
Samuel told all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.
He said, "This is what the king who rules over you will do: He will take your sons and make them serve with his chariots and horses, and they will run in front of his chariots.
He will make some of them commanders of thousands and of fifties. Others will plough his fields and harvest his crops, and others will make weapons of war and parts for his chariots.
He will take your daughters to make perfume and to cook and bake.
He will take the best of your fields, vineyards and olive groves and give them to his officials.
He will take a tenth of your grain and of your grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
He will take your male and female servants, your best young men and your donkeys, and use them for his own work.
He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his slaves.
When that day comes, you will cry out because of the king you have chosen, but the LORD will not answer you in that day."
But the people refused to listen to Samuel. "No!" they said. "We want a king over us.
Then we will be like all the other nations, with a king to lead us and to go out in front of us and fight our battles."
When Samuel heard everything the people said, he repeated it to the LORD.
The LORD answered, "Listen to them and give them a king." Then Samuel said to the Israelites, "Everyone go back to your own town."
